significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(ii) causal conclusion that LLMs contain partially separable "own-belief" and "attributed-belief" representations, and that leakage from the former causes false-belief attribution errors that can be reduced by removing the own-belief component. This establishes both a phenomenon—error-trial readouts "shift toward the own-belief value"—and a mechanism for the information-access failures behaviorally studied in FANToM (Kim et al., 2023), but it remains bounded to one error class rather than providing a law across behaviors or scales. Verified false would distinguishably rule out this two-channel leakage account, although because the hypothesis conjoins separability, leakage, and causal repair, refutation would not by itself identify which premise failed. After substituting the claim with the generic LLM-belief topic, I would not retain this score: the self/other causal decomposition is the claim-specific increment, but its separable-direction-plus-repair form keeps it only modestly above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "leakage metric" and the training-free intervention "own-belief subspace ablation"; the former is chiefly a post-hoc diagnostic, while the latter acts ex ante at the attribution position before the erroneous answer is produced. After re-extraction on another model, the claim predicts a directional relation—greater own-to-other leakage should accompany more attribution error and projection should reduce it—but supplies no quantitative scaling or threshold, so model-specific substantive details still require rediscovery. The hypothesis speaks broadly of "LLMs" and information-asymmetry scenarios, making researchers and potentially practitioners deploying theory-of-mind systems downstream, though its own prompt-sensitivity caveat and lack of an asserted cross-architecture invariance limit that scope. Topic substitution would remove the specific leakage metric and inference-time ablation and therefore would not preserve this score; those handles, especially the pre-output intervention, are what raise its reach above a generic belief-representation study.
